decisions.title: Ready for your close-up
decisions.situation: Leonie points a phone camera at you. You can see yourself on the screen. Your nose deserves further investigation.

choices.label: Move right up to the lens
Wave at the small person on screen
Turn around at the crucial moment

result.title: Mostly nostril
result.body: Leonie keeps the picture. It is a bold choice of composition.

journal.text: I gave Leonie a very close view of my nose.

decisions.title: Who invited that baby?
decisions.situation: There is a baby in the mirror. They copy every move you make. You have concerns about their manners.

choices.label: Pull your strangest face
Look behind the mirror
Wave hello

result.title: Extremely rude guest
result.body: They pull it right back. You laugh and try another one.

journal.text: I made faces at my reflection and laughed when it copied me.

decisions.title: Something under the blanket
decisions.situation: You tell Leonie there is a dragon under your blanket. Leonie asks whether it would like a bedtime story.

choices.label: Make room for one more listener
Invent the dragon’s entire biography
Ask Leonie to check properly

result.title: A civilised dragon
result.body: The dragon listens very quietly. Leonie does all the voices.

journal.text: My imaginary dragon joined bedtime stories.

decisions.title: Heavy traffic
decisions.situation: A caterpillar is crossing a path. It has a lot of feet and very little urgency.

choices.label: Crouch down and watch
Give it plenty of room
Challenge it to a race

result.title: Eventually, the other side
result.body: It reaches the edge and disappears under a leaf. You remain impressed by all the feet.

journal.text: I watched a caterpillar cross a path.

decisions.title: The invisible exhibit
decisions.situation: You forgot your show-and-tell. Mia has already announced that yours is “the best one”. Everyone turns towards your empty hands.

choices.label: Admit you left it at home
Act out an escaped dinosaur
Claim it is invisible and dangerous

result.title: A disappointing lack of magic
result.body: Leonie lets you describe it. Mia whispers that the publicity may have been a mistake.

journal.text: I admitted forgetting my show-and-tell object.

decisions.title: The handle is no longer involved
decisions.situation: You knock Leonie’s favourite mug off the table. The handle leaves the rest of the mug. Nobody saw.

choices.label: Tell Leonie what happened
Offer to help repair it
Slide the evidence behind a plant

result.title: Bad news, delivered properly
result.body: Leonie is disappointed about the mug and pleased you said something.

journal.text: I admitted breaking Leonie’s mug.

decisions.title: The wrong caption
decisions.situation: Your classroom display has Mia’s label under your drawing and yours under a picture of a potato. Leonie is about to show the class.

choices.label: Point out the swap quietly
Introduce your new potato portrait
Accuse Mia of stealing credit

result.title: Labels corrected
result.body: Leonie swaps the labels before the display. The potato keeps its anonymity.

journal.text: I quietly pointed out swapped labels on a classroom display.

decisions.title: A complaint from past you
decisions.situation: You find a childhood letter addressed to yourself. It says, “If you are not a dinosaur by thirteen, you have ruined everything.” There is a drawing of the expected dinosaur.

choices.label: Make a tail out of socks and deliver a roar
Write a formal rejection on the back
Destroy the evidence

result.title: Partial compliance
result.body: The tail falls off during your first turn. You add “technical difficulties” beneath the original demand and draw yourself with better knees.

journal.text: I answered a childhood demand to become a dinosaur by making a sock tail.

decisions.title: The helmet knows too much
decisions.situation: Mia built a “mind-reading helmet” from a colander. Luca wants a demonstration. You are supposed to feed Mia the answers with hand signals.

choices.label: Suggest an actual test instead
Deliver the hand signals theatrically
Claim the mind-reading genius was yours

result.title: The colander fails peer review
result.body: You test questions neither of you has rehearsed. The helmet reads no minds. Luca appreciates the method; Mia dislikes your timing.

journal.text: I tested Mia’s fake mind-reading helmet honestly.

decisions.title: Answers attached
decisions.situation: Mia sends you a photo of tomorrow’s homework answers. Their message says “delete after reading”, which sounds very normal.

choices.label: Do your own work
Offer to work through it together
Copy it, including the wrong date

result.title: Less convenient
result.body: You work through the questions. You understand the method by the end.

journal.text: I did my own homework after Mia sent a photo of the answers.

decisions.title: The microphone is still on
decisions.situation: After a class announcement, Mia whispers that the school jingle sounds like a microwave. The microphone is still on.

choices.label: Switch it off and warn them
Help make a short apology
Add microwave sound effects

result.title: Broadcast ends
result.body: Most people heard the first comment. You prevent a second one.

journal.text: I switched off a live microphone before Mia said anything worse.

decisions.title: The soup tribunal
decisions.situation: You describe a bowl of soup online as “fine”. A stranger accuses you of destroying local culture. They have posted eleven replies and a diagram.

choices.label: Explain that you meant the soup
Leave the soup to its lawyers
Publish a detailed attack on their diagram

result.title: A narrow defence
result.body: You clarify that your review concerns lunch rather than civilisation. The diagram receives no further comment.

journal.text: I clarified a soup review after a stranger took it personally.

decisions.title: The naked gardener
decisions.situation: The community garden in Hamburg needs volunteers. Its organiser is wearing a novelty apron printed with a naked torso and refuses to explain it.

choices.label: Weed beside the alarming apron
Ask about the plants, very specifically
Decide you have seen enough nature

result.title: A productive misunderstanding
result.body: You clear a whole bed. Three passers-by stop to stare before realising the torso has pockets.

journal.text: I volunteered beside a gardener in an alarming novelty apron in Hamburg.

decisions.title: The lost hand
decisions.situation: You pick up a glove from a bench. A rubber hand slides out of its sleeve. It has painted fingernails, a wristwatch and no obvious owner.

choices.label: Carry it to reception
Leave it upright on the bench
Ask around for anyone missing a hand

result.title: Please wave if this is yours
result.body: The receptionist holds the hand above the counter. A magician hurries over, thanks you and immediately removes its thumb. You stop watching.

journal.text: I returned a magician’s rubber hand to reception.

decisions.title: Your shoulders have a complaint
decisions.situation: After sitting in the same position for a while, you notice that your shoulders appear to have crept up towards your ears.

choices.label: Take a gentle movement break
Change your position and relax your shoulders
Stay exactly as you are

result.title: A different position helps
result.body: You loosen up at a comfortable pace and return to what you were doing. You had not noticed how stiff you were.

journal.text: I took a gentle movement break after sitting still.

decisions.title: The important businessman
decisions.situation: You sit in the last free café chair. A child wearing an enormous tie tells you it is reserved for an important businessman. The businessman, they explain, is them.

choices.label: Ask what business they are in
Offer them the chair after your drink
Explain that reserving chairs is bad business

result.title: A volatile juice market
result.body: They explain that juice has gone up and crayons are a bad investment. You move to the counter while they hold a meeting with a biscuit.

journal.text: I gave up a café chair after hearing a child’s business plan.

choices.label: Ask what the label means
Step back and let them stop it
Ask whether smoke costs extra

result.title: A useful admission
result.body: The volunteer stops and explains the failed mechanism. You learn more from the mistake than from the planned demonstration.

journal.text: I asked about a warning label during a failed toy-repair demonstration.

decisions.title: You need medical attention
decisions.situation: Your symptoms have become serious: persistent worry and disrupted sleep. A hospital assessment can begin treatment and may require a short stay. The quoted care costs €20.00; an unpaid emergency bill remains a real obligation.

choices.label: Accept hospital assessment
Decline assessment

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

decisions.title: Wealth you cannot see
decisions.situation: A free gallery in Hamburg displays an empty plinth titled “My Invisible Yacht”. A visitor says only rich people can understand it. You can see the same amount of yacht as everyone else.

choices.label: Ask the guide what the work means
Admire its excellent fuel economy
Pretend to fall overboard

result.title: A surprisingly useful explanation
result.body: The guide says it is about status and imaginary ownership. The visitor looks relieved that somebody has supplied an answer.

journal.text: I asked about an invisible-yacht artwork in Hamburg.

result.title: Medical care arranged

decisions.title: In loving memory of the wrong man

choices.label: Suggest checking the plaque first
Hear the allegedly deceased man out
Leave before the eulogy

result.title: Death withdrawn from the proposal
result.body: You help redirect the discussion towards correcting the inscription. The man asks to keep “much loved” if possible.

journal.text: I suggested correcting a memorial plaque for a living man in Hamburg.

decisions.title: A reminder that needs reminding

choices.label: Write a clearer private reminder
Work backwards from the context
Assume it will make sense later

result.title: Future you gets better information
result.body: You replace the riddle with a useful explanation and keep it somewhere appropriate.

journal.text: I replaced an unhelpful private reminder with a clear one.

decisions.title: One missed intention

choices.label: Take the next manageable step
Ask whether the intention needs adjusting
Declare yourself hopeless at consistency

result.title: A smaller conclusion
result.body: You treat the missed moment as one moment and carry on with what you can manage now.

journal.text: I avoided turning a small missed intention into a verdict on everything.

decisions.title: A striking resemblance
decisions.situation: A caricaturist at a street fair in Hamburg offers you a free sample portrait. A small crowd gathers. The artist turns the drawing around. It is you as an enormous angry thumb.

choices.label: Ask whether they could add a jawline
Ask for a pencil and draw the artist
Cover the portrait and leave

result.title: The formal thumb
result.body: The artist adds a bow tie. You point out that this is not a jawline. A spectator says the resemblance is uncanny. You leave holding a thumb in evening wear.

journal.text: I asked a caricaturist to correct my portrait and received a thumb in a bow tie.

choices.label: Deflate it before it reaches the doorway
Climb in and ask for paddles
Insist the picture on the box was misleading

result.title: A long public fart
result.body: You open the valve. The canoe collapses over eight uninterrupted seconds of rude noise. The instructor waits until everyone has stopped laughing to explain the warning.

journal.text: I deflated a full-size canoe during a crowded craft workshop.

journal.text: I heard the story behind an old photo. Leonie also confessed to approving the haircut.

choices.label: Celebrate without the comparison chart
Choose one goal that is actually yours
Read every biography before bed

result.title: Cake remains an achievement
result.body: You put the list aside. Your day improves immediately when it stops competing with a dead inventor.

journal.text: I ignored an unhelpful achievement list on my birthday.

choices.label: Thank them, then admit it is not yours
Point out the actual poet’s name
Accept the praise and invent your inspiration

result.title: A narrow escape from poetry
result.body: They laugh at the mix-up. You both admit you were not entirely sure what the last line meant.

journal.text: I corrected a stranger who thought I had written a poem.

decisions.title: The song of extra garlic
decisions.situation: At a community singalong, the lyric projector fails. It starts displaying a takeaway receipt instead. The backing track continues. Everyone looks to you for the first line.

choices.label: Sing the receipt with feeling
Pass the microphone down the row
Demand that they restore the proper words

result.title: Hold the onions
result.body: You hit the high note on “extra garlic”. The room joins in for “delivery instructions”. The organiser finally switches off the projector during the sauce options.

journal.text: I led a singalong using a takeaway receipt as the lyrics.

choices.label: Say you will wait for a peer-reviewed vegetable
Ask to see the potato’s qualifications
Buy the supposed cure — €599.92

result.title: The potato is unavailable for questions
result.body: They offer to remove the sprouts at no extra charge. You end the conversation before discussing the postgraduate options.

journal.text: I declined a supposed potato cure for Anxiety disorder.

choices.label: Explain that it is a garden cleanup
Delete the post without explaining
Add “No questions. Bring gloves.”

result.title: The photographs help
result.body: You attach a photo of weeds and broken plant pots. Two people volunteer. A third asks for a picture of you holding today’s newspaper. You decline that part.

journal.text: I explained a suspicious shopping list attached to my garden-cleanup request.

decisions.title: A beautiful baby cabbage
decisions.situation: A fair organiser needs one more judge for a vegetable baby contest. Someone pushes a cabbage in a bonnet towards you. Its grower is waiting for a score and looks ready to take this personally.

choices.label: Judge the cabbage’s personality
Disclose that you eat cabbage
Give it a terrible score for poor eye contact

result.title: A quiet, grounded child
result.body: You praise its composure and excellent leaves. The grower wipes away a tear. A rival arrives with a swaddled turnip and demands equal time.

journal.text: I praised a bonnet-wearing cabbage at a vegetable baby contest.

decisions.title: The door does not believe in you
decisions.situation: An automatic shop door refuses to open for you. It opens for a child, a trolley and a blowing receipt. You step forward. Nothing. The cashier points at the sensor and suggests waving.

choices.label: Ask the cashier to let you out
Follow the trolley out
Perform an increasingly furious dance

result.title: Assisted departure
result.body: The cashier walks over. The doors open immediately for them. They hold the sensor while you leave, like a bouncer escorting out a ghost.

journal.text: I had to ask a cashier to release me through an automatic door.

Claim you meant your own wig
Keep reopening the chat in horror

result.title: An honest public disaster

journal.text: I apologised after sending a rude wig comment to a group chat.

Enjoy feeling well without a quota
Fill every bit of the day

result.title: A useful day with an ending
result.body: You use some energy without treating all of it as a resource that must be exhausted.

journal.text: I paced a good day instead of filling every available moment.

Deliver a speech about surviving the last ice age

result.title: A breakthrough in reverse ageing

Let another questioner take this one
Announce that the pigeons work for you

journal.text: I questioned the evidence behind a speaker’s theory about pigeons.

choices.label: Write back about the sheet
List what you did achieve
Send your younger self a furious reply

result.title: The corners remain hostile
result.body: You report that the elastic corners remain a problem. You omit finances; you are not being interrogated by a child with a felt-tip pen.

journal.text: I answered an old note about being wealthy and folding fitted sheets.

Time the swing and walk through slowly
Sprint straight through the swinging axe

result.title: A head start
result.body: You turn back. A speaker announces, “The coward flees!” Three visitors turn to look. You continue with your head and your dignity approximately intact.

journal.text: I took the long route around a museum’s mechanical executioner.

decisions.situation: The community garden in Hamburg needs volunteers. Its organiser is wearing a novelty apron printed with a naked torso and refuses to explain it.

choices.label: Weed beside the alarming apron
Ask about the plants, very specifically
Decide you have seen enough nature

result.title: A productive misunderstanding
result.body: You clear a whole bed. Three passers-by stop to stare before realising the torso has pockets.

decisions.title: A number with nowhere to go
decisions.situation: You suddenly remember a telephone number you have not used for years. You cannot remember what you entered a room to fetch, but the number is perfect.

choices.label: Enjoy the memory’s strange priorities
Return calmly to the original task
Treat the distraction as a personal crisis

result.title: An impressive useless recital
result.body: You repeat the number once and laugh at the timing. Memory has supplied an answer to a question nobody asked.

journal.text: I remembered an old telephone number at an unhelpful moment.

decisions.title: What do you do all day?
decisions.situation: A stranger assumes you are retired and asks whether you have taken up “something gentle, like birdwatching”. You have not told them anything about your life.

choices.label: Tell them what your days actually involve
Say the birds are frightened of you
Describe every activity they failed to imagine

result.title: An overdue factual check
result.body: You give a short answer. They apologise for inventing your schedule before learning your name.

journal.text: I corrected a stranger’s assumption about my daily life.

decisions.title: One missed intention
decisions.situation: You miss a small personal intention and catch yourself declaring the whole effort ruined. The declaration is much larger than the missed step.

choices.label: Take the next manageable step
Ask whether the intention needs adjusting
Declare yourself hopeless at consistency

result.title: A smaller conclusion
result.body: You treat the missed moment as one moment and carry on with what you can manage now.

journal.text: I avoided turning a small missed intention into a verdict on everything.

decisions.title: You are almost in the picture
decisions.situation: An old photograph catches you at the edge of the frame, apparently concentrating on something outside it. You can no longer remember what seemed so important.

choices.label: Enjoy the unfinished little mystery
Write down what you do remember
Build a grand explanation around the pose

result.title: A life outside the frame
result.body: You let the unknown detail remain unknown. The photograph still holds an ordinary moment worth keeping.

journal.text: I enjoyed an old photograph without solving every detail.

decisions.title: The sofa is judging you

choices.label: Switch to the beginner version and try it
